methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops led by a Norfolk native represent grassroots capacity-building in a non-metro hub, signaling potential for distributed deep learning if community-led models can scale beyond individual initiatives.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's formal partnership with AI Ready RVA creates institutional infrastructure for AI education and innovation, but concentration in the state capital raises questions about whether knowledge diffuses beyond the Richmond metro region.

signals.title: More than 30,000 customers await broadband connections as provider struggles to complete work
signals.signal_reading: Over 30,000 customers in Southside and Central Virginia still awaiting basic broadband demonstrates infrastructure failure that prevents even shallow AI adoption, deepening the digital divide while metros advance.

signals.title: EPA grant backs community-driven workforce training in Southwest Virginia - Virginia Tech News
signals.signal_reading: EPA-funded community-driven workforce training in Southwest Virginia suggests bottom-up capability development in an underserved region, though success depends on whether training yields deep skills or surface-level platform use.

signals.title: Children’s National and Virginia Tech deepen pediatric AI collaboration to accelerate innovation for children - Children's National Hospital
signals.signal_reading: Children's National and Virginia Tech pediatric AI collaboration concentrates advanced R&D capability in the New River Valley tech corridor, leveraging university assets but creating a specialized excellence pocket rather than distributed capacity.
